Darren, I was told at Visa HQ we only need a "business letter" for the girls...the requirements are below from 
their website....However, what Karyna has sent is from the Japanese consulate website. The Visa HQ people said 
we only need the "business letter" I really don't know what the correct answer is here. But I would think the 
more we have the better.: 
htt v//japan.visahq.cotn/requirements/Russia/resident-United_Stateslitijapan-business-visa 
From Visa HQ: 
Business Letter. A business letter from the sending company in the US. The letter should be printed on the 
company letterhead stationery, addressed to the Embassy of Japan, Visa Section, Washington DC, and signed by a 
senior manager (an equivalent to Vice-President or above). The business letter must adhere to the following 
guidelines: 
• Briefly introduce the applicant (please specify employment status/position held in the company by applicant). 
• State the nature of the business to be conducted (ie. business meetings, contract negotiations, etc.) and the 
names and addresses of companies to be contacted in Japan. 
• Specify the type and desired validity of the visa (ie. multiple entry business visa). 
• Guarantee of sufficient funds for travel. 
From Karyna from the Japanese consulate website: 
If traveling for BUSINESS, original letter from applicant's company signed by an authorized executive officer, on company 
letterhead, stating: 
a) applicant's position in the company 
b) duration of employment 
c) nature/purpose of visit in detail 
d) dates/duration of stay intended 
e) contact person, company name, address and phone number of business contact in Japan 
f) guarantee of financial support during applicants stay in Japan and return transportation from Japan

in paragraph (1) in the clause that starts on the second line midway on the line with "Interested in

change "as well and" to "as well as".

has been seeking for collaboration on investments in startups in Japan." I would change "seeking 
for collaboration" to "seeking collaboration".

Hi =I 
Thank you so much for the employment letters you left for us. Japanese consulate seem to be very particular 
with their rules, I copied below the requirements they list on their website regarding company's letters: 
If traveling for BUSINESS, original letter from applicants company signed by an authorized executive officer, on company 
letterhead, stating: 
a) applicants position in the company 
b) duration of employment 
c) nature/purpose of visit in detail 
d) dates/duration of stay intended 
e) contact person, company name, address and phone number of business contact in Japan 
f) guarantee of financial support during applicants stay in Japan and return transportation from Japan 
Looks like we are missing the following in 
letters: 
- applicant's position (it describes the duties, but does not mention "executive assistant" as our position) 
- duration of employment

Hi 
Thank you so much for the employment letters you left for us. Japanese consulate seem to be very particular 
with their rules, I copied below the requirements they list on their website regarding company's letters: 
If traveling for BUSINESS, original letter from applicant's company signed by an authorized executive officer, on company 
letterhead, stating: 
a) applicant's position in the company 
b) duration of employment 
c) nature/purpose of visit in detail 
d) dates/duration of stay intended 
e) contact person, company name, address and phone number of business contact in Japan 
f) guarantee of financial support during applicant's stay in Japan and return transportation from Japan 
Looks like we are missing the following in 
letters: 
- applicant's position (it describes the duties, but does not mention "executive assistant" as our position) 
- duration of employment 
I don't know if that will cause a problem at all, but to be safe can you please ask Darren (if he is the one who 
wrote the letters) if he could re-write them including the two things mentioned above?

well as".

"seeking collaboration". 
Nothing else jumped out at me.

Checking the website of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, I have found the attached detailed 
info of the procedure. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
I) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs, etc" 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
*Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not, Joi can ask 
one of Japanese companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-
General of Japan in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/about/emb_cons/over/index.html 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close 
relationship with Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html

As you can see on the file with the details of the visa procedure for Russians, which I have

is almost the same as the business visa.

trip schedule, instead of a Japanese company for a business visa.

option.

b) 2 photos

*Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not, Joi can ask 
one of Japanese companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-
General of Japan in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/about/emb_cons/over/index.html 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close 
relationship with Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
*Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name , date of birth and male/female 
II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), 
accommodations on each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
*Btw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/short/novisa.html

We have not worked on the procedure of Japanese visa for those with Russian passports before but we would 
love to be any help of yours. 
Checking the website of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, I have found the attached detailed 
info of the procedure. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
I) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs, etc" 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
*Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not, Joi can ask 
one of Japanese companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-
General of Japan in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/about/emb_cons/over/index.html 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close 
relationship with Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jpikinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
*Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name , date of birth and male/female 
II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), 
accommodations on each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
*Btw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j_info/visiUvisa/short/novisa.html

1) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs. etc 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
'Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not. Joi can ask one of Japanese 
companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-General of Japan in 
the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/about/emb constover/index.htrn1 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close relationship with Japanese 
companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j  info/visitivisa/short/russia nis.html

II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), accommodations on 
each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to.

2015/04/14 16:26, Mika Tanaka Nakano 
Iii 
Thank you for your mail. 
We have not worked on the procedure of Japanese visa for those with Russian passports before but we would love to be any 
help of yours. 
Checking the website of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, I have found the attached detailed info of the 
procedure. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j  info/visit/visalshortlrussia nis.html 
1) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs. etc 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
'Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not. Joi can ask one of Japanese 
companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-General of Japan in 
the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/about/emb cons/over/index.html 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close relationship with 
Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j  info/visitivisaishortkussia nis.html 
Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name . date of birth and male/female 
II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), accommodations on 
each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
'Btw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.godpi  info/visitivisaishortMovisa.html

2015/04/14 16:26, Mika Tanaka Nakano 
Iii 
Thank you for your mail. 
We have not worked on the procedure of Japanese visa for those with Russian passports before but we would love to be any 
help of yours. 
Checking the website of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, I have found the attached detailed info of the 
procedure. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j  info/visitivisaishort/russia nis.html 
1) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs. etc 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
'Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not. Joi can ask one of Japanese 
companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-General of Japan 
in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/about/emb constover/index.html 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close relationship with 
Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j  info/visitivisaishort/russia nis.html 
'Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name . date of birth and male/female 
II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), accommodations 
on each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
*Blw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/  info/visitivisa/short/novisa.htrnl 
Thank you! 
Best regards, 
Mika

Hi Lesley, 
As you can see on the file with the details of the visa procedure for Russians, which I have downloaded

the business visa. 
The difference is that a Japanese travel agency needs to be a host and issue all those letters and trip 
schedule, instead of a Japanese company for a business visa. 
If you can hire a Japanese travel agency somehow for booking their travels, that can be an option. 
But since we don't know any agency in Japan, we can't help for tourist visa.

Hi Lesley, 
As you can see on the file with the details of the visa procedure for Russians, which I have downloaded 
for you, from the Japanese Foreign Ministry site, the procedure for the tourist visa is almost the same as 
the business visa. 
The difference is that a Japanese travel agency needs to be a host and issue all those letters and trip 
schedule, instead of a Japanese company for a business visa. 
If you can hire a Japanese travel agency somehow for booking their travels, that can be an option. 
But since we don't know any agency in Japan, we can't help for tourist visa. 
There's no simple tourist visa for Russians in Japan, unfortunately.

Hi Lesley, 
As you can see on the file with the details of the visa procedure for Russians, which I have 
downloaded for you, from the Japanese Foreign Ministry site, the procedure for the tourist visa is 
almost the same as the business visa. 
The difference is that a Japanese travel agency needs to be a host and issue all those letters and trip 
schedule, instead of a Japanese company for a business visa. 
If you can hire a Japanese travel agency somehow for booking their travels, that can be an option. 
But since we don't know any agency in Japan, we can't help for tourist visa. 
There's no simple tourist visa for Russians in Japan, unfortunately.

Hi 
Thank you for your mail. 
We have not worked on the procedure of Japanese visa for those with Russian passports before but we would 
love to be any help of yours. 
Checking the website of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, I have found the attached detailed 
info of the procedure. 
http://www.mofa.gojp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
I) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs, etc" 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
*Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not, Joi can ask one 
of Japanese companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-
General of Japan in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.m.jp/about/emb_cons/over/indez.html 
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close 
relationship with Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.gojp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
*Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name , date of birth and male/female 
II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), 
accommodations on each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
EFTA00349565
--- PAGE 2 ---
*Btw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/novisa.html 
Thank you! 
Best regards, 
Mika

Here is the info from Joi Ito's office re a visa for a russian passport holder. Please have a look ... 
Begin forwarded message: 
From: Mika Tanaka Nakano < 
Subject: Re: Jeffrey Epstein 
Date: A ril 14, 2015 at 3:26:21 AM EDT 
To: 
Cc: Heather deManbey < 
Hi 
Thank you for your mail. 
We have not worked on the procedure of Japanese visa for those with Russian passports before but we would 
love to be any help of yours. 
Checking the website of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, I have found the attached detailed 
info of the procedure. 
http://www.mofa.gojp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
1) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs, etc" 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
*Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not, Joi can ask one 
of Japanese companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-
General of Japan in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.gojp/about/emb_cons/over/indez.html 
EFTA00349621
--- PAGE 2 ---
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close 
relationship with Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
*Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name , date of birth and male/female 
ID Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), 
accommodations on each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
*Btw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/novisa.html 
Thank you!

Mika

Intermediary Disclosure. Amex assists you in finding travel suppliers and making arrangements that 
meet your individual needs. We consider various factors in identifying travel suppliers to you and 
recommending specific itineraries. In this role, we are acting as an independent third party and not 
as a fiduciary. We want you to be aware that certain suppliers pay us commissions as well as

incentives to our travel counselors. Certain suppliers may also provide compensation to us for 
various marketing and administrative services that we perform for them, such as granting them 
access to our marketing channels, participating in marketing programs and supporting technology 
initiatives. In addition, we receive compensation from suppliers when customers use the American 
Express Card or other American Express products to pay for supplier products and services. From 
time to time we may enter into other business relationships with suppliers and these arrangements, 
including levels and types of compensation and incentives we receive, are subject to change. In 
identifying suppliers and recommending itineraries, we may consider a number of factors, including 
supplier availability and your preferences. The relationships we have with suppliers may also 
influence the suppliers we identify and the itineraries we recommend.
